title: Bonalu
description: Bonalu is the Hindu festival honouring the goddess Mahankali in Hyderabad's old city — one of the clearest signs of the Deccan's plural festival calendar, drawing Muslim shopkeepers as readily as Hindu families.
dedication: In memory of the Asaf Jahi dynasty
subtitle: Hyderabad · Old City

items.value: Draws Muslim shopkeepers as readily as Hindu families

blocks.intro: Bonalu is the Hindu festival honouring the goddess Mahankali, celebrated in Hyderabad's old city. It stands among the clearest signs of the Deccan's plural festival calendar: a Hindu observance that draws Muslim shopkeepers as readily as Hindu families.

sections.sub: A Hindu observance rooted in the old city
body: Bonalu honours the goddess Mahankali in the old city of Hyderabad, one of the observances that make up the wider Hindu strand of the Deccan's festival year alongside Bathukamma and Ugadi.<cite data-ref="eaton-2005"></cite>

sections.sub: One of the clearest signs of Hyderabad's plural festival year
body: Hyderabad's festivals are remarkably plural, and Bonalu is one of the clearest examples: it draws Muslim shopkeepers as readily as Hindu families, standing alongside the urs at Gulbarga and Yousufain Sharif and the Deccan Festival each February as evidence of a shared civic calendar rather than separate ones.<cite data-ref="eaton-2005"></cite>

references.text: Richard M. Eaton, A Social History of the Deccan, 1300–1761: Eight Indian Lives, Cambridge University Press, 2005.
